title: Memory Mosaics at scale
summary: Exhaustive verification of 'Memory Mosaics at scale' (paper id 20777) completed in lenient mode. The paper was segmented into 68 typed snippets (10 display equations, 32 figure references, 13 tables, 13 text sections/subsections incl. appendix) and routed to specialist verifiers: math verification on equations 1-10, statistical verification on the quantitative tables (Tables 1-5, 9, 12, 13), citation verification on the reference list and in-text citations, text verification on all prose sections, and a final cross-section consistency pass over the full paper. All verifiers returned NO_ERROR. The math equations are algebraically consistent (e.g., Eq. 6 adaptive bandwidth beta = beta_1*n^alpha + beta_0 is consistent with the stated MISE motivation 1/sqrt(beta) ~ n^{-1/(p+4)} and with the accompanying prose 'the larger the effective bandwidth adaptation'). Statistical checks confirmed all table averages (Table 1 avg 52.2/52.2; Table 2 56.8 vs 56.6; Table 9 42.1 vs 34.9) and claimed gaps (4k: 1.4%-5.6%; 32k: 12.3%-14.8%; 8T transformer lag of 6.5%) are internally consistent. Citation verification confirmed key references (Zhang 2025 AI-for-the-Open-World arXiv:2504.14751, Zhang et al. 2025 Memory Mosaics ICLR 2025, Beck et al. xLSTM NeurIPS 2024, Hsieh et al. RULER arXiv:2404.06654) are genuine, correctly attributed works; the in-text 'Beck et al., 2025' vs. reference year 2024 is a benign minor year discrepancy, not a fabricated citation. Text and cross-section consistency checks found no fatal internal contradictions: the abstract's claims match the body's nuanced findings, and the Figure 6 caption ('starts to match' on semantic ICL) versus Section 6.1 ('data scaling alone cannot close the gap' on new-knowledge QA) refer to distinct evaluation dimensions and are presented coherently. No critical errors requiring correction were detected.
